title: Grateful Dead Live at University of Virginia on 1982-09-14
lineage: 1st Set: Beyer M160 -> Cassette Master (Sony D5) -> Dat -> CD -> EAC -> SHN2nd Set: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Reel -> Dat -> CD -> EAC -> SHN

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a scorching 1982 Charlottesville show with a smoking second set highlighted by the China Cat > Rider transition and Space‑Aiko jam.
ai_review.review: The recording is a solid sound‑board mix that most listeners describe as clear and well balanced, with only occasional mic‑hiss on a few tracks. Musically the concert is a fan favorite – the first set rolls along nicely while the second set erupts into high‑energy jams, especially the China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider segue, the Space → Aiko improvisation and fiery renditions of High Time, He's Gone, Bertha and Johnny B. Goode. Overall the performance is praised as hot, tight and unforgettable despite a sweltering venue.

ai_rating.rationale: The overwhelming majority of reviews are 5‑star with consistent praise for both the musical performance and the soundboard quality; only a few minor criticisms appear, supporting a high rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally crisp and well balanced; some reviewers note occasional mic noise (‘bacon frying’) on Jack Straw but overall the SBD captures the band clearly, even allowing decent bass presence.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: Typical early‑80s two‑set layout with a tight first set and an extended, jam‑heavy second set that builds to a climactic finish; the flow is praised for its seamless transitions.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly lauded for his sweet tone, hot playing on High Time, and leading the space jam with Bob.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for ‘smoking’ a stage monitor at the end of Rider; several reviewers comment that Phil’s bass is audible and powerful in this mix.
band_member_comments.Bob: Featured prominently in the Space → Aiko jam and quoted before Johnny B. Goode, praised for his vocal and guitar contributions.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent (keyboards) singled out for strong playing during China Cat Sunflower and its transition into Rider; overall keyboards are described as solid.
